evidence.explanation: The raised lactate in the third patient, which was in cerebrospinal fluid rather than blood and was found through his seizure work-up.

steps/12.description: Raised lactate in blood, cerebrospinal fluid or both in three of the four children. Subject 1 reached 9.3 and then over 20 mmol per litre in blood; subject 3 had CSF lactate of 5.0 and later 5.6 against a normal below 2.4; subject 4 had blood lactate of 16.9 to 18.5 and CSF lactate of 10.9. Subject 2 had normal lactate in blood and CSF, but magnetic resonance spectroscopy showed elevated lactate in multiple brain areas.

evidence.snippet: Cranial MRI undertaken at just over 36 hr of age demonstrated a diffusely abnormal signal intensity of the entire supratenterial white matter and decreased cortical folding for her age
evidence.explanation: The white-matter lesion in the first patient at 36 hours of life, which is the earliest imaging in the series.

evidence.snippet: On follow-up MRI, the brain abnormalities were less swollen, did not enhance, and displayed partial cystic degeneration and white-matter volume loss
evidence.explanation: The evolution of the white-matter lesion in the second patient over years.

steps/13.description: White-matter disease on MRI in three of the four children: diffusely abnormal supratentorial white matter with brainstem and cerebellar involvement at 36 hours in subject 1, extensive progressive supratentorial lesions including the corpus callosum with later cystic degeneration and volume loss in subject 2, and corticospinal tract, brainstem and thalamic changes in subject 4.

evidence.snippet: Investigation of his seizure disorder revealed elevated CSF lactate (5.0 mmol/L; normal < 2.4 mmol/L) and increased T2 signal in the basal ganglia on cranial MRI.
evidence.explanation: The basal ganglia finding in the third patient at five months.

evidence.snippet: Re-evaluation of his symptoms included repeat cranial MRI, which confirmed progressive changes involving the deep cortical gray matter of the basal ganglia as well as a more diffuse atrophic process.
evidence.explanation: That the same patient's basal ganglia lesion progressed, which is what makes it a degenerative process rather than a static finding.

steps/14.description: Basal ganglia involvement on MRI in two of the four children: increased T2 signal in the basal ganglia in subject 3, with progressive changes in the deep cortical grey matter on repeat imaging, and basal ganglia lesions as part of the disseminated picture in subject 2.

evidence.snippet: At 2.5 years, he was bedridden and was unable to walk, grasp, or speak.
evidence.explanation: The extent of the regression in the second patient after a febrile trigger.

evidence.snippet: it was clear that he had lost previously acquired developmental skills and was exhibiting truncal hypotonia with limb and facial dystonia
evidence.explanation: The regression in the third patient, recognised during a status epilepticus admission.

steps/15.description: Loss of acquired skills in two of the four children. Subject 2 walked independently at 16 months, deteriorated after an unexplained fever at 25 months and by 2.5 years was bedridden and unable to walk, grasp or speak; he then partially recovered. Subject 3 developed normally until three months and had clearly lost acquired skills by five months, at the time of a status epilepticus admission.

evidence.snippet: At 3 weeks old, he became extremely irritable but continued to develop normally until 3 months, when he experienced an explosive onset of seizures.
evidence.explanation: The onset in the third patient, and the normal development that preceded it.

evidence.snippet: At 7 weeks, she was admitted to the hospital after displaying a series of unusual movements suggestive of a seizure disorder.
evidence.explanation: The presentation of the fourth patient.

evidence.snippet: Cerebral function monitoring (amplitude-integrated electroencephalography) showed a significantly suppressed baseline and no detectable seizure pattern.
evidence.explanation: The documented negative in the first patient, which is why the band is FREQUENT rather than higher.

steps/16.description: Seizures in two of the four children, and in both they dominate the course. Subject 3 had an explosive onset of seizures at three months that remained problematic despite medical treatment; subject 4 was admitted at seven weeks with a series of unusual movements suggestive of a seizure disorder.

evidence.snippet: At 5 months old, after being admitted to the hospital for status epilepticus, it was clear that he had lost previously acquired developmental skills
evidence.explanation: Status epilepticus as the admission that revealed the third patient's regression.

evidence.snippet: She gradually deteriorated as a result of status epilepticus, apnoea episodes, and persistent lactic acidosis.
evidence.explanation: Status epilepticus as part of the terminal course in the fourth patient.

steps/17.description: Status epilepticus in the two children with seizures, and in both it was a turning point: subject 3 was admitted with it at five months, which is when his regression was recognised, and subject 4 deteriorated with it before her death at 13 weeks.

evidence.snippet: Further motor regression and rapid onset of spasticity of all four limbs followed.
evidence.explanation: The onset of the spasticity, and the regression it followed.

evidence.snippet: Over the last 2 years, he has lost all voluntary movement in his limbs.
evidence.explanation: The endpoint of the motor course at the time of report.

steps/18.description: Rapid onset of spasticity of all four limbs in subject 2 at around 25 months, following motor regression. It has dominated his subsequent course: dysarthric speech and wheelchair dependency from seven years, and loss of all voluntary limb movement over the two years before the report. He is managed with an intrathecal baclofen pump and three-monthly botulinum toxin injections.

evidence.snippet: it was clear that he had lost previously acquired developmental skills and was exhibiting truncal hypotonia with limb and facial dystonia
evidence.explanation: The tone examination in the third patient, with the dystonia and its distribution.

steps/19.description: Limb and facial dystonia with truncal hypotonia in subject 3 at five months, recognised at the same admission as his developmental regression.

evidence.snippet: Vison is impaired as a result of optic atrophy, whereas hearing is normal.
evidence.explanation: The optic finding in the second patient, in the same sentence as the negative hearing assessment that bounds his sensory involvement. The typographical error in the first word is the source's, and the quote is reproduced as printed.

evidence.snippet: Vision is significantly impaired in relation to bilateral optic atrophy.
evidence.explanation: The same finding in the third patient at ten years.

steps/20.description: Bilateral optic atrophy in both long-surviving children. Subject 2's vision is impaired by optic atrophy while his hearing is normal; subject 3's vision is significantly impaired in relation to bilateral optic atrophy at ten years.

evidence.snippet: By 5 years, his hair had grown thicker and more diffusely on his scalp, although head growth was poor (0.4th percentile) and development remained markedly delayed in all domains.
evidence.explanation: The delay across all domains at five years, with the poor head growth alongside it.

evidence.snippet: At his current age of 10 years, he sits independently but is unable to stand or walk.
evidence.explanation: The functional level five years later, which shows the delay is persistent rather than transient.

steps/21.description: Development markedly delayed in all domains in subject 3 at five years, and still so at ten: he sits independently but cannot stand or walk, and is mute though he responds positively to familiar voices.

evidence.snippet: Clinical examination demonstrated severe generalized hypotonia and absent primitive reflexes.
evidence.explanation: The neurological examination in the first patient in her first day of life.

steps/22.description: Severe generalized hypotonia with absent primitive reflexes in subject 1 on the day of birth, examined during her terminal deterioration.

evidence.snippet: He developed swallowing difficulties and required a gastrostomy tube for feeding.
evidence.explanation: The feeding problem and the intervention it required in the second patient.

evidence.snippet: he also suffered significant gastro-esophageal reflux with multiple episodes of aspiration pneumonia to the extent that by 2.5 years, he had developed bronchiectasis
evidence.explanation: The different feeding problem in the third patient, and the structural lung damage that followed it.

steps/23.description: Swallowing difficulty requiring a gastrostomy tube in subject 2 during his regression, and significant gastro-oesophageal reflux with repeated aspiration pneumonia in subject 3, severe enough that he had bronchiectasis by 2.5 years.

evidence.snippet: a capillary blood gas at that time revealed metabolic acidosis (pH = 7.12, lactate = 5.9 mmol/L, BE = −10.2) and hypoglycaemia (blood glucose = 1.2 mmol/L)
evidence.explanation: The hypoglycaemia and the acidosis it accompanied, in the first hour of life.

steps/24.description: Persistent neonatal hypoglycaemia in subject 1, first at a blood glucose of 1.2 mmol per litre within an hour of birth and still present after a dextrose infusion was started.

evidence.snippet: Repeat blood analyses revealed clotting abnormalities, hyperammonaemia (129 μM; normal < 100 μM), and a rising blood lactate (9.3 mmol/L; normal < 2.2 mmol/L).
evidence.explanation: The ammonia measurement with its reference interval, and the findings it accompanied.

steps/25.description: Raised blood ammonia at 129 micromolar against a normal below 100 in subject 1, found with clotting abnormalities and a rising lactate during her terminal deterioration.

edges/10.description: Pyruvate that cannot be oxidised is reduced to lactate to regenerate NAD+, which is the standard route from a complex I block to a lactic acidosis.

edges/12.description: Optic atrophy is a recurrent feature of complex I disease and is present in the two long-surviving patients here, but nothing in the source traces it from the respiratory defect, so the edge records an unexplained gap rather than a pathway.

edges/13.description: Recorded only in the neonate who also had abnormal clotting, a raised gamma-glutamyl transpeptidase and echogenic areas in the liver. The source does not link the hypoglycaemia to a mechanism, so this edge is a placement rather than an explanation.

edges/14.description: As for the hypoglycaemia: reported once, in the same neonate, in the same paragraph as the clotting abnormality, and not mechanistically traced by the source.

evidence.snippet: This study therefore establishes NDUFA6 as the 29th structural subunit of complex I to be associated with human pathology.
evidence.explanation: The gene-disease relationship as established, and its novelty at the time.

evidence.snippet: Subsequent analysis by BN-PAGE confirmed that transduction of all three subject cell lines with a wild-type NDUFA6 cDNA transcript ameliorated the complex I assembly defect, unequivocally establishing the subjects’ NDUFA6 variants as the cause of disease
evidence.explanation: The complementation result that converts an association into a causal claim, in all three cell lines available.

evidence.snippet: Genotype-Tissue Expression (GTEx) data and in-house RNA-seq data19 support ENST00000602404.5 as the predominant isoform
evidence.explanation: The transcript finding behind the RefSeq revision, which is what makes variant numbering in this gene transcript-dependent.

evidence.snippet: In summary, there is moderate evidence to support the relationship between NDUFA6 and autosomal recessive NDUFA6 -related primary mitochondrial disease.
evidence.explanation: The independent strength-of-evidence judgement, which is Moderate rather than Definitive and is a fair reflection of a single four-family series with strong functional data.

genes/0.notes:
NDUFA6 encodes NADH:ubiquinone oxidoreductase subunit A6, also known as LYRM6, a 15 kDa accessory subunit of the complex I Q-module whose LYR motif binds the mitochondrial acyl carrier protein NDUFAB1. The 2018 report establishes it as the 29th structural subunit of complex I linked to human disease.
A transcript trap, which the paper itself is largely about. NDUFA6 has three in-frame isoforms using alternative initiation methionines, and the consensus RefSeq accession did not correspond to the predominant transcript in clinically relevant tissues; the paper's expression data prompted the revision of the reference accession to NM_002490.5. This is not a bookkeeping detail. Subject 3's start-loss allele is pathogenic against the predominant short transcript and would read as a tolerated p.Met27Ile missense change against the longer one, which is the authors' candidate explanation for his normal muscle complex I activity. Anyone re-interpreting a variant in this gene has to state which transcript they are numbering against.
A Named Entity Confusion trap, which dominates a naive literature search. NDUFA6 carries a large common-variant and expression-signature literature that has nothing to do with this disease: a missense variant reported to confer schizophrenia risk, bioinformatic hub-gene analyses in tetralogy of Fallot, multiple myeloma, glioma, thyroid cancer, sepsis and preeclampsia, a lncRNA named NDUFA6-DT, and a ceramide-NDUFA6 interaction in liver ischaemia-reperfusion injury. None of it is cited here and none of it concerns MC1DN33.

evidence.snippet: He has an implanted pump for intrathecal Baclofen therapy and receives Botox injections every 3 months.
evidence.explanation: The two tone-directed treatments this patient receives, and the interval at which the second is given.

treatments/0.description: Subject 2 has an implanted pump delivering intrathecal baclofen for the four-limb spasticity that followed his regression. It is symptomatic management of tone, not treatment of the complex I defect, and no outcome is reported for it.

treatments/0/targets/0.description: Baclofen is a GABA-B agonist given intrathecally to reduce spastic tone. It acts on the symptom and on nothing upstream of it, which is why the effect is recorded as modulation rather than restoration of anything.

evidence.snippet: He developed swallowing difficulties and required a gastrostomy tube for feeding.
evidence.explanation: The intervention and the problem that prompted it.

treatments/1.description: Subject 2 developed swallowing difficulties during his regression and required a gastrostomy tube for feeding. Securing enteral nutrition around an unsafe swallow is standard supportive management in a progressive mitochondrial encephalopathy, and it is the only feeding intervention recorded in this series.

evidence.snippet: Long-standing neutropenia, first noted at 2 years, was treated with granulocyte colony-stimulating factor.
evidence.explanation: The treatment and the indication for it, in the one patient who received it.

treatments/2.description: Subject 3's long-standing neutropenia, first noted at two years, was treated with granulocyte colony-stimulating factor. Like the tone and feeding measures, this addresses a complication rather than the respiratory chain defect, and no outcome is reported.

evidence.snippet: the situation for subject 3—normal enzymatic activity in muscle despite a demonstrable complex I assembly defect—is most unusual
evidence.explanation: The observation itself, with the authors' own assessment of how odd it is.

evidence.snippet: The existence of the longer NDUFA6 isoform (UniProt: P56556) could explain the normal complex I activity reported for subject 3, whose variant would instead act as a homozygous missense variant in the encoding transcript (c.81G>A [p.Met27Ile]).
evidence.explanation: The first candidate explanation, at the strength the authors give it.

evidence.snippet: Attempts to assess whether an alternative methionine was selected for translation initiation in vivo have been unsuccessful; analysis of tryptic fragments of subject proteins produced during complexome profiling was uninformative, and commercially available antibodies have failed to conjugate successfully with the target protein in subject and control tissues
evidence.explanation: Why the question is open rather than answered: both routes to testing it were tried and both failed for technical reasons.

open_questions/0.rationale:
Subject 3 is homozygous for c.3G>A, which abolishes the initiation methionine of the predominant transcript, and yet his muscle complex I enzymology was normal. His fibroblasts nonetheless showed a marked isolated assembly defect on blue native electrophoresis, and failed to grow when forced onto oxidative phosphorylation in galactose medium. The authors call the combination most unusual and say so plainly: it is common for fibroblasts to look normal when muscle is deficient, but the reverse is not.
Two explanations are offered and neither is settled. The first is the longer NDUFA6 isoform: against transcript NM_002490.4 the same nucleotide change reads as p.Met27Ile, which in silico tools call tolerated, so if the long isoform is expressed in muscle it would supply functional protein there. The second is leaky initiation, where translation starts at various in-frame methionines and Met1- and Met27-containing polypeptides coexist, diluting the effect. Both were tested as far as the available methods allowed and neither could be confirmed: tryptic fragments from complexome profiling were uninformative about which methionine was used, and the antibodies available did not work on the target protein in either subject or control tissue.
This is not an academic point. It is the reason a normal muscle complex I assay does not exclude MC1DN33, which is the diagnostic conclusion the paper itself draws, and it is why any reinterpretation of a variant in this gene has to state its transcript.

evidence.snippet: A clear reduction of N-module subunits was visible, particularly in the most severely affected individual, subject 1 (Figure 4B, boxed area), correlating the assembly defect with the observed phenotypic severity.
evidence.explanation: The correlation the authors draw between assembly-defect depth and clinical severity.

evidence.snippet: Subject 1, who presented with the most aggressive clinical course, had the most marked reduction in fully assembled complex I, whereas subjects 2 and 3 (whose presentations were less severe) also had impaired complex I assembly, although to a lesser extent.
evidence.explanation: The same gradient measured on blue native electrophoresis, which is the second independent assay to show it.

evidence.snippet: In fact, investigation of cDNA from fibroblasts showed a normal amount of NDUFA6 transcript
evidence.explanation: Why the surviving patient's frameshift allele is not a transcript-level null, which is part of why allele class alone does not order the severity.

open_questions/1.rationale:
The four reported children span almost the whole range a mitochondrial disease can span. Two died in infancy of unrelenting lactic acidosis, at 51 hours and 13 weeks. Two are alive years later, one with a slowly progressive spastic leukoencephalopathy and preserved cognition, the other with an epileptic encephalopathy and basal ganglia disease.
Something does track with severity at the cellular level. Complexome profiling shows the reduction of N-module subunits was most marked in subject 1, the child who died fastest, and the loss of NDUFA7 and NDUFA12 correlated with the degree of NDUFA6 loss; her respirometry was remarkably impaired where the other two were near control. So biochemical depth and clinical severity move together across the series.
What that does not do is explain the range from the genotype. Subject 1 carries a missense and a nonsense allele; subject 4, who also died in infancy, carries two frameshifts; subject 2, who survived, carries a homozygous frameshift predicted to escape nonsense-mediated decay and confirmed to produce normal transcript levels. A severity ordering read off allele class alone would not put subjects 2 and 4 on opposite sides of the line. With four patients, one report and no functional data at all from subject 4, the honest position is that the modifier is unidentified rather than that the genotype explains it.

evidence.snippet: Seizures remained problematic despite medical treatment, and he also suffered significant gastro-esophageal reflux with multiple episodes of aspiration pneumonia
evidence.explanation: The one explicit statement about treatment response in the series, and it is a failure of symptomatic control rather than a disease-modifying result.

evidence.snippet: Despite intensive-care management in a tertiary care center, her lactic acidosis continued until her death at 13 weeks of age.
evidence.explanation: What maximal supportive care achieved in the fourth patient, which is the closest the source comes to a treatment outcome.

open_questions/2.rationale:
No. Nothing disease-modifying is reported for any of these four children, no treatment response is described, and no trial has been registered for the gene or the disorder.
What the treatments block holds is the three symptomatic measures the paper actually records, each in one patient: intrathecal baclofen and botulinum toxin for spasticity, a gastrostomy tube for an unsafe swallow, and granulocyte colony-stimulating factor for neutropenia. All three address complications, none is reported with an outcome, and one of the two treated children is severely disabled while the other has drug-resistant seizures. They are curated because they are documented facts about these patients, not because they amount to a management strategy. The intensive care both dying infants received - inotropes, fresh frozen plasma, transfusion, bicarbonate, ventilation - is described in the progression block rather than curated as treatment, because the source records it as a level of care rather than as intervention with an indication.
The lentiviral complementation is not a treatment. It is the experiment that established causality, it is curated under experimental_models with its limitations, and the authors present it as proof of pathogenicity. Reading it as gene therapy in prospect would be an inference the source does not make.
Generic supportive management of mitochondrial encephalopathy is ready-made content that would look right here and is deliberately not imported. Asserting of four NDUFA6 patients an experience recorded only of other people with other genotypes would make the entry look more complete and be less true.

evidence.snippet: Episodes of infection-triggered metabolic deterioration, observed in her first years of life9, had resolved.
evidence.explanation: Establishes infection as the trigger of the metabolic episodes, and that they resolved with age.

evidence.snippet: Here, we describe a patient with a homozygous p.Tyr12Cys mutation in the epsilon subunit encoded by the nuclear gene ATP5E.
evidence.explanation: Identifies the causal allele and gene in the index patient.

evidence.snippet: The subunit epsilon of mitochondrial ATP synthase is the only F1 subunit without a homolog in bacteria and chloroplasts and represents the least characterized F1 subunit of the mammalian enzyme.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the structural singularity of the epsilon subunit that makes this lesion distinct from other F1 subunit defects.

steps/2.description: A single allele accounts for the whole disease: c.35A>G, replacing the highly conserved tyrosine at position 12 of the epsilon subunit with cysteine, homozygous in all three reported patients and absent from controls. Epsilon is the smallest F1 subunit and the only one with no bacterial or chloroplast homologue, sitting in the central stalk with gamma and delta. The mutant protein is made and is incorporated into the enzyme — this is not a null allele — but its presence depresses the biosynthesis of the complex.

evidence.snippet: The mitochondrial content of the ATP synthase complex was equally reduced, but its size was normal and it contained the mutated epsilon subunit.
evidence.explanation: Establishes that the deficiency is of enzyme amount, with the assembled enzyme structurally normal and carrying the mutant subunit.

evidence.snippet: Our results indicate an essential role of the epsilon subunit in the biosynthesis and assembly of the F1 part of the ATP synthase.
evidence.explanation: The authors' conclusion assigning epsilon an assembly role rather than a catalytic one.

evidence.snippet: Silencing of the ATP5E gene in HEK293 cells resulted in downregulation of the activity and content of the mitochondrial ATP synthase complex and of ADP-stimulated respiration to approximately 40% of the control.
evidence.explanation: Independent knockdown reproduces the reduced enzyme content and activity without a patient allele.

evidence.snippet: The contents of both ATP synthase subunits and of fully assembled complex V were severely reduced.
evidence.explanation: Independent restatement of the reduced content of assembled complex V; graded OTHER as a review summary.

steps/3.description: The primary biochemical lesion is a shortage of assembled enzyme, not a broken enzyme. Mitochondrial content of the ATP synthase complex falls by 60-70 percent in patient fibroblasts, matching the fall in activity; the complex that is present is of normal size and contains the mutant epsilon subunit, and it hydrolyses and synthesises normally. F1 and Fo subunits fall together, and the reduction of the assembled 600 kDa complex is not accompanied by F1 subcomplexes — the enzyme fails to be built rather than falling apart after assembly. Silencing ATP5F1E in HEK293 cells reproduces this without any patient allele, confirming that reduced epsilon dosage alone is sufficient.

evidence.snippet: A similar reduction was found in all investigated F1 and Fo subunits with the exception of Fo subunit c, which was found to accumulate in a detergent-insoluble form.
evidence.explanation: The defining asymmetry — subunit c accumulates while every other subunit falls.

evidence.snippet: The subunit c was present in the full-size ATP synthase complex and in subcomplexes of 200-400 kDa that neither contained the F1 subunits, nor the Fo subunits.
evidence.explanation: Resolves the accumulated subunit c into orphan subcomplexes in the knockdown model.

evidence.snippet: The results indicate that the epsilon subunit is essential for the assembly of F1 and plays an important role in the incorporation of the hydrophobic subunit c into the F1-c oligomer rotor of the mitochondrial ATP synthase complex.
evidence.explanation: States the c-ring loading role that this node asserts.

evidence.snippet: Unlike the expression of the other subunits, the c subunit was found to accumulate and aggregate in a detergent-insoluble form, an accumulation that was also described in other disorders, such as Batten disease and fragile X syndrome, which will be discussed below.
evidence.explanation: Independently restates the selective detergent-insoluble accumulation of subunit c and places it alongside the same accumulation in Batten disease and fragile X syndrome; graded OTHER as a review synthesis.

steps/4.description: The one asymmetry in the biochemistry, and the reason this lesion says something about enzyme biogenesis. Every investigated F1 and Fo subunit falls in proportion to the assembled complex except subunit c, which instead accumulates in a detergent-insoluble form. The same accumulation appears in ATP5F1E-silenced HEK293 cells, where subunit c is found in 200-400 kDa subcomplexes containing neither F1 nor other Fo subunits. This implicates the epsilon subunit in loading the hydrophobic c-ring onto the rotor, a role distinct from stabilising F1.

evidence.snippet: Patient fibroblasts showed 60-70% decrease in both oligomycin-sensitive ATPase activity and mitochondrial ATP synthesis.
evidence.explanation: Quantifies the functional deficit in patient cells.

evidence.snippet: In the patient fibroblasts decreased activities of ATP synthase and ADP-stimulated respiration with increased mitochondrial membrane potential at state 3-ADP were found, indicating an insufficient capacity of ATP synthase.
evidence.explanation: Adds the reduced ADP-stimulated respiration and the raised membrane potential; graded OTHER as a review summary of the index study.

steps/5.description: Oligomycin-sensitive ATPase activity and mitochondrial ATP synthesis both fall by 60-70 percent in patient fibroblasts, in step with the loss of assembled enzyme. ADP-stimulated respiration is reduced and the mitochondrial membrane potential is raised under state-3 conditions, the pattern expected when the proton gradient is generated normally but cannot be discharged through a sufficient number of ATP synthases.

evidence.snippet: So far, mitochondrial diseases caused by isolated disorders of the ATP synthase have been shown to result from mutations in mtDNA genes for the subunits ATP6 and ATP8 or in nuclear genes encoding the biogenesis factors TMEM70 and ATPAF2.
evidence.explanation: Frames the entity as an isolated ATP synthase disorder and names the pre-existing causes it was added to; graded OTHER because this background sentence reports no experiment.

evidence.snippet: In support of these findings, fluorescence staining of OXPHOS proteins in fibroblasts from patient 2 revealed markedly decreased amounts of the ATPase marker ATP5F1A relative to controls
evidence.explanation: Independent confirmation of reduced ATP synthase amount in a second patient's fibroblasts.

steps/6.description:
This node exists to state the boundary of the entity. The ATP5F1E lesion is an ISOLATED complex V deficiency: the electron-transport complexes are not reduced, and in the index patient's fibroblasts they were increased, an apparently compensatory change that does not rescue the energetic defect. That is what separates MC5DN3 from the combined-OXPHOS presentations in which complex V deficiency is one component among several, and it is the biochemical signature that points a diagnostic workup at the nuclear ATP-synthase genes.
Conformance note: the module node pairs decreased oxidative phosphorylation with increased reactive oxygen species. Only the first half is evidenced here. A ROS increase is a reasonable inference from the raised state-3 membrane potential, and the same review that reports that potential makes the electron-leak argument - but it demonstrates the ROS rise in TMEM70-lacking fibroblasts, not in ATP5F1E ones, so the ROS arm is not asserted. The module's upstream node, age-related mitochondrial damage and mtDNA mutation, does not apply to a primary nuclear-gene subunit defect, so conformance is declared at this node alone.

evidence.snippet: The 22-year-old woman presented with neonatal onset, lactic acidosis, 3-methylglutaconic aciduria, mild mental retardation and developed peripheral neuropathy.
evidence.explanation: Lactic acidosis from the neonatal period in the index patient.

evidence.snippet: Patient 3, a 13-year-old girl, was evaluated for intellectual disability, gait ataxia, and peripheral neuropathy. During infancy, she manifested lactic acidosis with transient respiratory failure, developmental delay, and episodes of generalized tonic-clonic seizures.
evidence.explanation: Infantile lactic acidosis in a second unrelated patient with the same genotype.

steps/7.description: The presenting abnormality in all three patients, beginning in the neonatal period or infancy. In the index patient and in patient 3 the metabolic episodes were infection-triggered and resolved with age; in patient 2 they improved spontaneously.

evidence.snippet: The 22-year-old woman presented with neonatal onset, lactic acidosis, 3-methylglutaconic aciduria, mild mental retardation and developed peripheral neuropathy.
evidence.explanation: 3-methylglutaconic aciduria in the index patient.

steps/8.description: Documented in the index patient. 3-methylglutaconic aciduria is the organic aciduria that flags nuclear ATP-synthase and phospholipid-remodelling defects, and it was the screening handle used to look for further ATP5E patients.

evidence.snippet: Patient 3, a 13-year-old girl, was evaluated for intellectual disability, gait ataxia, and peripheral neuropathy. During infancy, she manifested lactic acidosis with transient respiratory failure, developmental delay, and episodes of generalized tonic-clonic seizures.
evidence.explanation: Developmental delay in infancy in patient 3, following the metabolic crisis.

steps/9.description: Developmental delay followed the neonatal or infantile metabolic crisis in both paediatric patients, preceding the intellectual disability recorded in all three.

evidence.snippet: In 2010, our group reported a specific ATP5F1E homozygous variant in a single patient with neuropathy, intellectual disability, and ataxia (MIM:614053)
evidence.explanation: Intellectual disability as one of the three cardinal persistent features of the index patient.

steps/10.description: Mild in the index patient and present in all three; in the two paediatric patients it followed a developmental delay that was itself preceded by the neonatal metabolic crisis.

evidence.snippet: we observed a non-progressive disease course with intellectual disability, ataxia, and axonal-demyelinating polyneuropathy; she had developed gait impairment with limb dystonia.
evidence.explanation: Characterises the neuropathy at 11-year follow-up of the index patient.

steps/11.description: Present in the index patient — characterised on long-term follow-up as an axonal-demyelinating polyneuropathy — and in patient 3. Patient 2 was described as having neuropathic signs within a dystonia-dominant picture.

evidence.snippet: Patient 3, a 13-year-old girl, was evaluated for intellectual disability, gait ataxia, and peripheral neuropathy. During infancy, she manifested lactic acidosis with transient respiratory failure, developmental delay, and episodes of generalized tonic-clonic seizures.
evidence.explanation: Gait ataxia in patient 3.

evidence.snippet: we observed a non-progressive disease course with intellectual disability, ataxia, and axonal-demyelinating polyneuropathy; she had developed gait impairment with limb dystonia.
evidence.explanation: The index patient's ataxia at 11-year follow-up, recorded as ataxia without a gait qualifier and separately from her gait impairment. The two evidence items together are why this record is bound to the parent HP:0001251 rather than to Gait ataxia.

steps/12.description: Gait ataxia in the index patient and in patient 3. It is a persistent feature rather than part of the acute metabolic episodes.

evidence.snippet: Metabolic abnormalities improved spontaneously, but she experienced development delay and progressively developed generalized dystonia with poor response to trialed medications; she also had visual and hearing deficits.
evidence.explanation: Generalised refractory dystonia in patient 2.

evidence.snippet: we observed a non-progressive disease course with intellectual disability, ataxia, and axonal-demyelinating polyneuropathy; she had developed gait impairment with limb dystonia.
evidence.explanation: Limb dystonia in the index patient. Generalized in one patient and limb in another is why this record is bound to the parent HP:0001332 rather than to Generalized dystonia.

steps/13.description: Limb dystonia with gait impairment in the index patient by her thirties, and generalised, medication-refractory dystonia in patient 2. Dystonia was the feature that brought several patients of the 2022 cohort to attention, since part of that cohort was ascertained from dystonia rather than mitochondrial disease registries.

evidence.snippet: Patient 2, a 16-month-old infant, presented after birth with vomiting, severe respiratory distress, seizures, and impaired consciousness associated with lactic acidosis.
evidence.explanation: Neonatal seizures with the metabolic crisis in patient 2.

steps/14.description: Seizures at presentation in patient 2 and generalised tonic-clonic seizures in infancy in patient 3. Not reported in the index patient.

evidence.snippet: Patient 2, a 16-month-old infant, presented after birth with vomiting, severe respiratory distress, seizures, and impaired consciousness associated with lactic acidosis.
evidence.explanation: Vomiting as a presenting feature of the neonatal metabolic crisis in patient 2.

steps/15.description: Vomiting opened the neonatal presentation in patient 2, as part of the metabolic decompensation rather than a primary gastrointestinal problem.

evidence.snippet: Patient 2, a 16-month-old infant, presented after birth with vomiting, severe respiratory distress, seizures, and impaired consciousness associated with lactic acidosis.
evidence.explanation: Impaired consciousness with the lactic acidosis in patient 2.

steps/16.description: Impaired consciousness accompanied the neonatal lactic acidosis in patient 2 - the encephalopathic component of the metabolic decompensation.

evidence.snippet: Patient 2, a 16-month-old infant, presented after birth with vomiting, severe respiratory distress, seizures, and impaired consciousness associated with lactic acidosis.
evidence.explanation: Severe neonatal respiratory distress in patient 2.

steps/17.description: Severe respiratory distress after birth in patient 2 and transient respiratory failure in infancy in patient 3, in both cases part of the neonatal or infantile metabolic decompensation rather than a primary lung disease.

evidence.snippet: Clinical phenotype started with early-onset lactic acidosis, 3-MGA, but no cardiac involvement, followed by mild mental retardation, exercise intolerance and peripheral neuropathy.
evidence.explanation: Lists exercise intolerance in the index patient's phenotype; graded OTHER as a review restatement.

steps/18.description: Reported in the index patient as part of the persistent phenotype.

evidence.snippet: Metabolic abnormalities improved spontaneously, but she experienced development delay and progressively developed generalized dystonia with poor response to trialed medications; she also had visual and hearing deficits.
evidence.explanation: Hearing deficit in patient 2; the same sentence records the visual deficit.

steps/19.description: Visual and hearing deficits were reported in patient 2 only. A single-patient observation within a three-patient disease.

evidence.snippet: Metabolic abnormalities improved spontaneously, but she experienced development delay and progressively developed generalized dystonia with poor response to trialed medications; she also had visual and hearing deficits.
evidence.explanation: Visual deficit in patient 2.

steps/20.description: Reported in patient 2 alongside the hearing deficit; not reported in the other two patients.

edges/1.description: The mutant epsilon subunit depresses biosynthesis of the enzyme, so less complex V is built.

edges/2.description: With too little epsilon, subunit c is not incorporated into the rotor and accumulates instead.

edges/3.description: Fewer assembled enzymes means less ATP synthesised, even though each enzyme works normally.

edges/4.description: The defect is confined to complex V; complexes I-IV are intact and in fact increased.

edges/5.description: Insufficient oxidative ATP production shifts the cell towards glycolysis with lactate accumulation.

edges/6.description: 3-methylglutaconic aciduria accompanies nuclear ATP-synthase deficiency, and is the organic-aciduria handle used to screen for these disorders. The metabolic route from the bioenergetic defect to the leucine-pathway intermediate is not resolved, here or in the better-studied TMEM70 and TAZ disorders.

edges/7.description: Reduced oxidative ATP capacity limits sustained skeletal-muscle work.

edges/8.description: Part of the neonatal metabolic decompensation; the intermediates are unknown.

edges/9.description: The encephalopathic component of the neonatal metabolic decompensation; the intermediates are unknown.

edges/10.description: Part of the neonatal and infantile metabolic decompensation rather than a primary lung defect; the intermediate steps between the energetic deficit and the respiratory presentation are not established.

edges/11.description: Developmental delay follows the neonatal or infantile metabolic crisis in the paediatric patients; the intermediates are unknown.

edges/12.description: The central nervous system is among the tissues least able to tolerate a shortfall in oxidative ATP supply, but no study has traced the route from the enzyme deficit to the cognitive outcome in this disease.

edges/13.description: A persistent neurological consequence of the energetic deficit; the anatomical substrate has not been imaged or examined in these patients.

edges/14.description: Movement-disorder consequence of the energetic deficit. The 2022 cohort makes the point that ATPase-subunit defects reach clinical attention through dystonia as often as through mitochondrial-disease pathways, but the intermediates are unknown.

edges/15.description: Seizures occurred with the neonatal and infantile metabolic decompensations; the intermediates are unknown.

edges/16.description: Long axons are a classic site of vulnerability to a chronic ATP shortfall, and neuropathy is one of the three persistent features of the index patient; the mechanism has not been studied in this disease.

edges/17.description: Reported in one of the three patients. Recorded as an edge because the sensory epithelia are energetically demanding, but with unknown intermediates and a single-patient basis.

edges/18.description: Reported in the same single patient as the hearing deficit, with the same caveats.

evidence.snippet: Episodes of infection-triggered metabolic deterioration, observed in her first years of life9, had resolved.
evidence.explanation: The only published statement tying an environmental trigger to the metabolic episodes in this disease.

edges/19.description: Infection raises energy demand and catabolic drive against an ATP synthase capacity that is already reduced by 60-70 percent, tipping a compensated deficit into a decompensated one. This is an exacerbation of an existing lesion, not a trigger of the disease, which is present from birth.

evidence.snippet: This is the first case of a mitochondrial disease due to a mutation in a nuclear encoded structural subunit of the ATP synthase.
evidence.explanation: Establishes ATP5F1E as the first nuclear structural-subunit cause of ATP synthase disease.

evidence.snippet: First, we were able to replicate ATP5F1E as a recessive disease gene in three unrelated patients, all of whom shared an identical homozygous variant.
evidence.explanation: Independent replication of ATP5F1E as a recessive disease gene.

genes/0.notes: ATP5F1E (formerly ATP5E; 20q13.32) encodes the epsilon subunit of the F1 catalytic head of mitochondrial ATP synthase — the smallest F1 subunit, part of the central stalk with gamma and delta, and the only F1 subunit with no bacterial or chloroplast homologue. Exactly one pathogenic allele is known: c.35A>G (p.Tyr12Cys), homozygous in all three reported patients from three unrelated families. The gene has a processed pseudogene, ATP5EP1, which is a practical consideration for primer design and read mapping.

evidence.snippet: Episodes of infection-triggered metabolic deterioration, observed in her first years of life9, had resolved.
evidence.explanation: Documents that the infection-triggered metabolic episodes resolved over an 11-year follow-up, which is what makes supportive management through the early years the substance of care.

treatments/0.description: No disease-modifying therapy exists. Management is the standard mitochondrial approach: treating acute lactic acidosis, avoiding and aggressively managing catabolic triggers such as intercurrent infection, and symptomatic care of the neurological features. It is worth recording that the metabolic instability in these patients improved with age in all three — spontaneously in patient 2 and with resolution of the infection-triggered episodes in the index patient — so the natural history of the metabolic component is towards stabilisation rather than progression.

evidence.snippet: Metabolic abnormalities improved spontaneously, but she experienced development delay and progressively developed generalized dystonia with poor response to trialed medications; she also had visual and hearing deficits.
evidence.explanation: Documents that symptomatic pharmacotherapy was attempted for the dystonia, which is the single claim this treatment record makes. The record makes no efficacy claim for the same quote to bear on, and the report names no agent, so no drug-specific claim is made here either. The poor response is recorded in the treatment description rather than graded as a second reading of one evidence item.

treatments/1.description: Dystonia is the feature most likely to need active treatment and the one that responded worst: in patient 2 the generalised dystonia responded poorly to the medications tried. No specific agent or class is recommended by the reports.

open_questions/0.rationale: Three patients, three families, one allele. That is enough for the 2022 group to call ATP5F1E replicated as a recessive disease gene, and the functional evidence is strong and independent of the allele — knockdown in HEK293 cells reproduces the biochemistry. But the same group had written a year earlier that the association "has not been firmly established", and the constraint is real: with a single recurrent variant, an allele-specific artefact and a shared founder haplotype cannot be excluded on genetics alone, and no genotype-phenotype range can be described because there is no second genotype. The practical consequence is that a laboratory finding a DIFFERENT biallelic ATP5F1E variant has no comparable case to reason from, and would need functional work to call it. Curating the entry is not in tension with the gap: the mechanism is well characterised, it is the allelic and phenotypic spectrum that is unknown.

evidence.snippet: Unlike the expression of the other subunits, the c subunit was found to accumulate and aggregate in a detergent-insoluble form, an accumulation that was also described in other disorders, such as Batten disease and fragile X syndrome, which will be discussed below.
evidence.explanation: The source for the observation this gap turns on - that the same detergent-insoluble subunit c accumulation occurs in Batten disease, one of the neuronal ceroid lipofuscinoses, and in fragile X syndrome. It is what makes the bystander-versus-injurious question worth asking, and it is a review's cross-disease observation rather than a measurement in an ATP5F1E patient.

open_questions/1.rationale: The selective accumulation of subunit c is the most distinctive feature of this lesion and the least followed up. Two readings are possible and the published data do not separate them. Either it is a bystander — surplus c-ring protein left over when there is not enough epsilon to load it, inert and simply a marker of where assembly stalls — or it is itself injurious, since insoluble accumulation of subunit c is the storage material of the neuronal ceroid lipofuscinoses and has been noted in other neurological disease. The distinction matters mechanistically: if the accumulated c is toxic then the disease has a proteinopathy arm that no current node captures, and subunit-c-directed readouts would belong in the diagnostic and therapeutic picture rather than only in the assembly story.

steps/2.description: From lymph nodes, virus disseminates via bloodstream to lymphoid organs, liver, and other tissues. Monocytes can be productively infected, potentially mediating systemic spread.

steps/3.description: MPXV encodes multiple immunomodulatory proteins that antagonize innate sensing (TLR, cGAS-STING), block interferon signaling (downregulation of STAT1, JAK2, IRF3), inhibit NF-κB activation, and impair dendritic cell maturation. NK cells expand but become functionally impaired.

steps/4.description: Epidermal keratinocytes undergo ballooning degeneration with cytoplasmic viral inclusions. Lesions evolve through characteristic stages - macule, papule, vesicle, pustule, and crust formation over approximately 3 weeks.

steps/5.description: MPXV replicates entirely in the host cytoplasm, forming ER-associated viral factories (Guarnieri bodies) where genome replication and virion assembly occur.

steps/6.description: The virus produces two infectious forms - intracellular mature virions (IMV) released by cell lysis, and extracellular enveloped virions (EEV) that acquire additional membrane for efficient cell-to-cell spread. Viral proteins F13L, B5R, A34R, and A36R orchestrate EEV formation and actin-based motility.

evidence.snippet: At least five MRX genes have been identified by positional cloning, but each accounts for only 0.5%-1.0% of MRX cases.
evidence.explanation: Quantifies the per-gene contribution, establishing that no single gene dominates this class.

evidence.snippet: The X-chromosome comprises only about 5% of the human genome but accounts for about 15% of the genes currently known to be associated with intellectual disability.
evidence.explanation: Quantifies the disproportionate contribution of the X chromosome to intellectual-disability genetics, the observation that motivated the field.

steps/22.description: Rare germline loss-of-function, hypomorphic, repeat-expansion, or copy-number variants in any one of a large set of genes on the X chromosome remove or reduce the activity of the encoded product in the developing and mature brain. The class is clinically homogeneous but genetically heterogeneous: variants at many different loci converge on the same single clinical outcome, and each individual gene accounts for only a small fraction of cases. The X chromosome is disproportionately represented among intellectual-disability genes relative to its size.

evidence.snippet: Because of the unbalanced sex ratio (1.3-1.4 to 1) observed in intellectual disability (ID) and the identification of large ID-affected families showing X-linked segregation, much attention has been focused on the genetics of X-linked ID (XLID).
evidence.explanation: Quantifies the male excess that hemizygous expression explains and that motivated the field's focus on the X chromosome.

evidence.snippet: This mosaic expression produces substantial complexity, especially when attempting to study the already complicated neural circuits that underly behavior, thus impeding the understanding of disease-related pathophysiology and the development of therapeutics.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the consequence of female mosaicism for mechanistic study and therapeutic development in this class. Tagged OTHER: the quoted sentence is a methodological statement about the difficulty of studying mosaic neural circuits, not a human clinical observation.

evidence.snippet: All carrier females with either point mutations or genomic deletions in FACL4 showed a completely skewed X-inactivation, suggesting that the gene influences survival advantage.
evidence.explanation: Demonstrates the complete X-inactivation skewing that spares carrier females in this class.

steps/23.description: Males carry one X chromosome, so a loss-of-function allele is expressed in every cell with no second copy to buffer it. Heterozygous females are mosaic, because random X-chromosome inactivation silences one X per cell, so the mutant allele is expressed in only a subset of cells; such carriers are typically unaffected or mildly affected, and in several subtypes completely skewed X-inactivation silences the mutant X entirely. This dosage asymmetry is the mechanistic basis of the male excess observed among people with intellectual disability, and the mosaicism is the principal obstacle to studying the circuit pathophysiology in females.

evidence.snippet: PAK proteins are crucial effectors linking Rho GTPases to cytoskeletal reorganization and to nuclear signalling.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the Rho GTPase-to-cytoskeleton arm of the convergence. Tagged OTHER: this is a background statement of established protein function, not a result generated by the cited study.

evidence.snippet: Signal transduction through Rho GTPases and PAK3 may be critical for human cognitive function.
evidence.explanation: Connects the Rho GTPase theme directly to the cognitive endpoint.

evidence.snippet: Rab GDP-dissociation inhibitors (GDI) are evolutionarily conserved proteins that play an essential role in the recycling of Rab GTPases required for vesicular transport through the secretory pathway.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the vesicle-trafficking arm of the convergence. Tagged OTHER: a background statement of established protein function rather than a result of the cited study.

evidence.snippet: tRNA modifications are crucial for efficient and accurate protein synthesis, and modification defects are frequently associated with disease.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the translational-fidelity arm of the convergence, which is mechanistically distinct from the synaptic-structural arms. Tagged OTHER: a general statement about tRNA biology rather than a result of the cited study.

evidence.snippet: These data implicate a crucial role for SLC9A7 in the regulation of TGN/post-Golgi pH homeostasis and glycosylation of exported cargo, which may underlie the cellular pathophysiology and neurodevelopmental deficits associated with this particular nonsyndromic form of X-linked ID.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the Golgi-pH/glycosylation arm of the convergence, the most recently characterised theme in this class.

evidence.snippet: Our results show that FMR2 is a potent transcription activator and that its function is conserved.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the transcriptional arm of the convergence and the molecular function lost when the FRAXE expansion silences AFF2/FMR2. Tagged IN_VITRO: the activation was measured in yeast and mammalian cell reporter assays. GO:0045893 (positive regulation of DNA-templated transcription) is used rather than the RNA-polymerase-II-specific term because the reporter assays demonstrate transcription activation without resolving promoter class.

evidence.snippet: Expansion of the FRAXE CCG repeat to a full mutation is associated with methylation and transcriptional silencing of the FMR2 gene, and as a consequence, mild-to-borderline mental retardation.
evidence.explanation: Connects the loss of that transcriptional activity to the cognitive endpoint, which is what places this arm on the convergence node rather than leaving it as isolated protein biochemistry. Tagged OTHER rather than HUMAN_CLINICAL: this is the abstract's opening background sentence, and the study itself reports no human clinical data (its MeSH terms are HeLa cells and Saccharomyces cerevisiae).

steps/24.description: Although the causal genes do not share a single pathway, their products fall repeatedly into a limited set of themes that converge on the same functional endpoint: Rho GTPase signalling to the actin cytoskeleton (PAK3), Rab-dependent synaptic vesicle recycling (GDI1), proposed roles in excitatory synapse formation and neurite outgrowth (IL1RAPL1, TSPAN7 - both inferred rather than directly demonstrated in the cited reports), tRNA anticodon-loop modification and translational fidelity (FTSJ1), fatty-acid metabolism (ACSL4), Golgi/trans-Golgi-network pH regulation and glycosylation (SLC9A7), transcriptional activation (AFF2, silenced by the FRAXE repeat expansion), and telencephalic transcriptional control (ARX). Most of these arms act on synapse formation, maintenance, and plasticity, and synaptic convergence is the field's dominant framing of the class. It is not, however, established for all of them: the tRNA-modification (FTSJ1), fatty-acid (ACSL4), Golgi-pH (SLC9A7), and transcriptional (AFF2) arms have documented molecular and cellular consequences but no cited evidence of a synaptic endpoint, so the node is deliberately named for neuronal rather than synaptic function. What is shared across every arm is that convergence happens at the level of neuronal cell biology rather than through a common molecular pathway - which is why no single pathway-directed therapy addresses the class. Enumerating the rest of the numbered series adds further themes without disturbing that conclusion: postsynaptic scaffolding at the NMDA receptor and the dendritic spine (DLG3, FRMPD4), synaptic vesicle clustering, mobility and cargo retrieval (SYN1, SYP), presynaptic terminal formation and maintenance from the Golgi (RAB39B), ubiquitin-proteasome substrate handling (MID2, KLHL15, USP27X), chromatin and transcriptional coregulation (ZNF711, ZMYM3), Arf-family guanine-nucleotide exchange (IQSEC2), serine-threonine kinase signalling (RPS6KA3) and microtubule stabilisation in developing neurons (FGF13). The ubiquitin arm is the clearest illustration that convergence here is thematic rather than directional: MID2 and KLHL15 are ubiquitin-ligase pathway components whose loss impairs degradation of specific substrates, whereas USP27X is a deubiquitinase, so the arm has no single direction and its process annotation deliberately carries no modifier. USP27X is also the one gene admitted here with essentially no characterised neuronal function, so for that arm this node records convergence without a mechanism.

evidence.snippet: Immunofluorescence analysis showed that PAK3 protein is highly expressed in postmitotic neurons of the developing and postnatal cerebral cortex and hippocampus.
evidence.explanation: Localises a causal gene product to the cortical and hippocampal circuits that carry the cognitive phenotype. Tagged MODEL_ORGANISM: the immunofluorescence was performed in animal tissue (the paper's MeSH terms include Mice and Rats), not in patients.

evidence.snippet: RNA in situ hybridization showed that TM4SF2 is highly expressed in the central nervous system, including the cerebral cortex and hippocampus.
evidence.explanation: Independent confirmation that causal genes in this class are enriched in the same learning-and-memory circuits. Tagged IN_VITRO: an in situ hybridisation tissue-expression assay rather than a clinical observation.

evidence.snippet: Our results show that both functional and developmental alterations in the neuron may account for the severe impairment of learning abilities as a consequence of mutations in GDI1, emphasizing its critical role in development of human intellectual and learning abilities.
evidence.explanation: Links the vesicle-recycling lesion to impaired learning through both functional and developmental neuronal alterations.

steps/25.description: The convergent synaptic lesion degrades activity-dependent plasticity in the hippocampal and cortical circuits that support learning and memory. Several causal genes are selectively or highly expressed in exactly these structures - IL1RAPL1 in the postnatal hippocampal memory system, PAK3 in postmitotic neurons of developing and postnatal cerebral cortex and hippocampus, TSPAN7 in cerebral cortex and hippocampus - which is the anatomical reason a diffuse molecular lesion produces a circumscribed cognitive phenotype.

evidence.snippet: MRI analysis showed no gross defects in brain development.
evidence.explanation: Documents the structurally normal brain that defines the non-syndromic endpoint.

evidence.snippet: The absence of detectable brain malformations in patients suggests that ARX may have an essential role, in mature neurons, required for the development of cognitive abilities.
evidence.explanation: Independent confirmation, in a second subtype, that the lesion is functional rather than malformative.

evidence.snippet: The present family supports the lack of additional phenotypic features in patients with GDI1 mutations, rendering a clinical diagnosis of GDI1-associated XLID impossible.
evidence.explanation: States the diagnostic consequence of a phenotype with no distinguishing features.

steps/26.description: The endpoint of the class: non-progressive impairment of intellectual functioning and adaptive behaviour in a brain that is structurally normal on imaging and free of any consistently reproducible dysmorphic, metabolic, or systemic sign. This is a mis-tuned rather than a mis-built or damaged circuit, which is why brain MRI is characteristically unremarkable and why - in the absence of any distinguishing feature - molecular testing rather than clinical recognition is the only route to a specific diagnosis. The class is conventionally described as static and non-progressive, with developmental regression arguing against the diagnosis; note that none of the evidence cited on this node speaks to temporal course, so the staticity claim rests on clinical convention rather than on a source quoted here.

evidence.snippet: Non-overlapping deletions and a nonsense mutation in this gene were identified in patients with cognitive impairment only.
evidence.explanation: Documents cognitive impairment as the sole clinical feature, which is the definition of the non-syndromic class. The VERY_FREQUENT band follows from the phenotype being definitional rather than variable.

evidence.snippet: the affected male family members had nonsyndromic intellectual disability, that is, they had neither abnormal body measurements nor any other significant clinical problems
evidence.explanation: Independent confirmation that intellectual disability is the isolated finding in a second subtype.

steps/27.description: Impaired intellectual functioning and adaptive behaviour, present as the only consistent shared feature of the class. Severity spans mild to severe depending on the gene and allele. Because the class aggregates many individually rare gene-defined disorders, severity cannot be meaningfully quantified at the group level.

edges/22.description: A variant on the single male X chromosome is expressed without a compensating allele. Note this edge encodes a dosage/conditioning relationship (hemizygosity is a property of male karyotype, not an event caused by the variant) rather than a downstream biochemical step; `DIRECT` is used because CausalLinkTypeEnum offers no conditioning value.

edges/23.description: Loss of the gene product in neurons impairs the synaptic processes it supports.

edges/24.description: Disrupted synapse formation, transmission, and recycling degrade activity-dependent plasticity.

edges/25.description: Degraded plasticity in an anatomically normal brain manifests as non-progressive intellectual disability.

evidence.snippet: Non-overlapping deletions and a nonsense mutation in this gene were identified in patients with cognitive impairment only.
evidence.explanation: Cognitive impairment as the sole clinical consequence of the molecular lesion, which is the claim this edge makes.

evidence.snippet: the affected male family members had nonsyndromic intellectual disability, that is, they had neither abnormal body measurements nor any other significant clinical problems
evidence.explanation: Independent confirmation in a second subtype that the endpoint presents as intellectual disability with nothing else attached.

edges/26.description: The clinical expression of this endpoint node. Impaired intellectual functioning is what the class is defined by, and in the strictest members of the series it is the only feature present, so the terminal mechanism node and this phenotype stand in a direct relation with no intervening step. The remaining phenotypes in this entry - global developmental delay, speech and language delay, behavioural and autistic features, and seizures - are deliberately left unwired: they appear in some subtypes and not others, and assigning each to a mechanism node requires per-subtype evidence this pass did not gather.

evidence.snippet: Thorough investigation of an MRX critical region in Xp22.1-21.3 enabled us to identify a new gene expressed in brain that is responsible for a non-specific form of X-linked mental retardation.
evidence.explanation: Establishes IL1RAPL1 as causal for the non-specific (non-syndromic) form.

genes/0.notes: Interleukin-1 receptor accessory protein-like 1 at Xp22.1-21.3. Deletions and nonsense variants cause non-syndromic X-linked intellectual disability; the protein is highly expressed in postnatal hippocampus and organises excitatory synapse formation.

evidence.snippet: The mutation produces premature termination, disrupting kinase function.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the loss-of-function mechanism of the causal PAK3 allele.

genes/1.notes: p21-activated serine-threonine kinase at Xq22. Truncating variants disrupt kinase function and abolish Rho GTPase-to-cytoskeleton signalling in postmitotic cortical and hippocampal neurons.

evidence.snippet: One of the mutations caused a non-conservative substitution (L92P) which reduced binding and recycling of RAB3A, the second was a null mutation.
evidence.explanation: Characterises both the missense and null mechanisms at this locus.

genes/2.notes: Rab GDP-dissociation inhibitor alpha. Missense (L92P) and null alleles impair recycling of RAB3A and synaptic vesicle traffic. Associated with a strictly non-syndromic phenotype across independent families.

evidence.snippet: Further investigation led to identification of TM4SF2 mutations in 2 of 33 other MRX families.
evidence.explanation: Provides the independent point-variant evidence beyond the index translocation.

genes/3.notes: Tetraspanin 7 (formerly TM4SF2) at Xp11.4, implicated by a disrupting X;2 translocation breakpoint and by point variants in MRX families.

evidence.snippet: Additionally, tRNA(Phe) from an NSXLID patient with a novel FTSJ1-p.A26P missense allele specifically lacks Gm34 , but has normal levels of Cm32 and o2yW37 .
evidence.explanation: Demonstrates allele-specific biochemical consequences at this locus.

genes/4.notes: tRNA 2'-O-methyltransferase, the human TRM7 homolog. Loss-of-function alleles abolish Cm32 and Gm34 modification of the tRNA anticodon loop; a p.A26P missense allele produces a selective Gm34 defect, giving an allele-specific biochemical readout.

evidence.snippet: Analysis of enzymatic activity in lymphoblastoid cell lines from affected individuals of both families revealed low levels compared with normal cells, indicating that both mutations are null mutations.
evidence.explanation: Provides the functional confirmation that both alleles are null.

genes/5.notes: Fatty acid-CoA ligase 4 (FACL4) at Xq22.3. Missense and splice-site null alleles reduce enzymatic activity in patient lymphoblastoid lines. Mapped by narrowing the ATS-MR contiguous-gene deletion interval to roughly 380 kb.

evidence.snippet: In contrast to other genes involved in XLMR, ARX expression is specific to the telencephalon and ventral thalamus.
evidence.explanation: Characterises the restricted expression domain that distinguishes ARX from the broadly expressed genes in this class.

genes/6.notes: Aristaless-related homeobox transcription factor with telencephalon- and ventral-thalamus-restricted expression. Polyalanine expansions and certain missense alleles give the non-syndromic phenotype modelled here; other alleles in the same gene cause distinct syndromic entities.

evidence.snippet: Sequence variants in 11 genes (KLF8, AFF2, SLC6A8, NDUFA1, ALG13, SRPX2, ATRX, NLGN3, FGDY, CDKL5, and NLGN4) have been found in families with IDX but in whom IDX numbers were never assigned.
evidence.explanation: Places AFF2 among the genes causing non-syndromal X-linked intellectual disability.

genes/7.notes: AF4/FMR2 family member 2 at the FRAXE folate-sensitive fragile site in Xq28. Silenced by CCG repeat expansion and methylation, giving the repeat-expansion route into this class. Found in non-syndromal (IDX) families that were never assigned an IDX number.

evidence.snippet: We report two unrelated families with multigenerational nonsyndromic intellectual disability (ID) segregating with a recurrent de novo missense variant (c.1543C>T:p.Leu515Phe) in the alkali cation/proton exchanger gene SLC9A7 (also commonly referred to as NHE7).
evidence.explanation: Establishes SLC9A7 as causal for a non-syndromic form in two independent families.

evidence.snippet: Mass spectrometry analysis of patient sera also revealed an abnormal N-glycosylation profile for transferrin, a clinical diagnostic marker for congenital disorders of glycosylation.
evidence.explanation: Provides a measurable biochemical readout for this form, unusual in a class defined by the absence of biochemical features.

genes/8.notes: Alkali cation/proton exchanger (NHE7) at Xp11.3, resident in the trans-Golgi network and post-Golgi vesicles. A recurrent p.Leu515Phe missense variant in two unrelated multigenerational families alkalinises the TGN and impairs N-glycosylation of exported cargo, with an abnormal serum transferrin glycosylation profile in patients. The most recently characterised mechanistic theme in this class; not curated as a formal subtype here because a corresponding MONDO descendant term was not confirmed.

evidence.snippet: The first family identified as having a nonsyndromic intellectual disability was mapped in 1988. Here we show that a mutation of IQSEC2, encoding a guanine nucleotide exchange factor for the ADP-ribosylation factor family of small GTPases, caused this disorder.
evidence.explanation: Establishes IQSEC2 as causal for the non-syndromic form and gives the protein function recorded in these notes.

genes/9.notes: IQ motif and Sec7 domain ArfGEF 2, a guanine nucleotide exchange factor for the ADP-ribosylation factor family of small GTPases. It is the causal gene of MRX1, the index family of the numbered series, found by systematic X-chromosome exome resequencing more than two decades after that family was mapped. The allelic spectrum reaches beyond isolated intellectual disability - MONDO carries "IQSEC2-related syndromic intellectual disability" among this term's exact synonyms - and those presentations are not curated here.

evidence.snippet: In two families, the clinical diagnosis had been nonsyndromic X-linked mental retardation.
evidence.explanation: Establishes that RPS6KA3 variants are found in families diagnosed as non-syndromic, which is what admits this gene to this entry.

evidence.snippet: The disorder is now recognized to be due to mutations in a serine threonine kinase RSK2(RPS6KA3) located at Xp22.2
evidence.explanation: Source for the kinase function and the Xp22.2 location recorded in these notes. Marked BACKGROUND because the sentence is the paper's introductory framing of previously established Coffin-Lowry genetics, not its own result.

genes/10.notes: Ribosomal protein S6 kinase, 90 kDa, polypeptide 3 (RSK2), a serine-threonine kinase located at Xp22.2. Single-amino-acid deletions and proximal-domain missense variants produce an attenuated, non-syndromic phenotype, while other alleles of the same gene cause Coffin-Lowry syndrome, curated separately in dismech.

evidence.snippet: We identified a missense mutation (c.236 C > G; p.S79W) in the SYN1 gene coding for synapsin I in the MRX50 family, affected by non-syndromic X-linked intellectual disability.
evidence.explanation: Establishes SYN1 as causal in the numbered MRX50 family with a non-syndromic presentation.

evidence.snippet: In addition, the presence of S79W Synapsin I strongly reduces the mobility of synaptic vesicles, with possible implications for the regulation of neurotransmitter release and synaptic plasticity.
evidence.explanation: The functional consequence of the causal allele recorded in these notes, demonstrated in cultured knockout hippocampal neurons.

genes/11.notes: Synapsin I, a neuronal phosphoprotein regulating neurotransmitter release and neuronal development. The MRX50 allele is a missense change in the B-domain region involved in recognition of highly curved membranes; it reduces synaptic vesicle mobility and increases vesicle clustering at presynaptic terminals. Distinct SYN1 alleles cause the epilepsy/autism entity curated separately as SYN1-Related_Disorder.

evidence.snippet: One mutation in family X (D-23) introduced a stop codon seven amino acids after the start codon (c.21C > A; p.Y7X). A second mutation, in the MRX72 family, altered the 5' splice site (c.215+1G > A) and normal splicing. Neither instance produced a protein.
evidence.explanation: Establishes both causal alleles and the loss-of-function mechanism recorded in these notes.

evidence.snippet: We show that RAB39B, a novel RAB GTPase of unknown function, is a neuronal-specific protein that is localized to the Golgi compartment.
evidence.explanation: Source for the protein family, neuronal specificity and Golgi localisation recorded in these notes and in the MRX72 subtype row.

genes/12.notes: A neuronal-specific small GTPase of the RAB family localised to the Golgi compartment. Null alleles - a near-start stop codon in one family and a 5' splice-site change in the MRX72 family - produce no protein, and downregulation reduces presynaptic boutons and disturbs neurite growth cones. The same gene is curated by ClinGen against an early-onset parkinsonism-intellectual disability syndrome (MONDO:0010709), a separate entity that is not curated here.

evidence.snippet: We have identified truncating mutations in the human DLG3 (neuroendocrine dlg) gene in 4 of 329 families with moderate to severe X-linked mental retardation.
evidence.explanation: Establishes DLG3 as causal, with the cohort yield that supports the gene assignment.

evidence.snippet: DLG3 encodes synapse-associated protein 102 (SAP102), a member of the membrane-associated guanylate kinase protein family.
evidence.explanation: Source for the protein identity and family recorded in these notes.

genes/13.notes: Discs large MAGUK scaffold protein 3, encoding synapse-associated protein 102 (SAP102), a membrane-associated guanylate kinase of the postsynaptic density of excitatory synapses whose PDZ domains bind the NR2 subunits of the NMDA receptor. Truncating alleles remove the third PDZ domain and are proposed to disrupt NMDA receptor targeting and signalling.

evidence.snippet: The screen has discovered nine genes implicated in XLMR, including SYP, ZNF711 and CASK reported here, confirming the power of this strategy.
evidence.explanation: The gene-discovery statement assigning SYP to X-linked intellectual disability.

evidence.snippet: Synaptophysin is an integral synaptic vesicle (SV) protein that accounts for ∼10% of total SV protein cargo.
evidence.explanation: Source for the protein identity and abundance recorded in these notes.

genes/14.notes: Synaptophysin, an integral synaptic vesicle protein that accounts for about a tenth of total synaptic vesicle protein cargo and is required for efficient retrieval of synaptobrevin II from the plasma membrane during endocytosis. Patient variants either mislocalise throughout the axon or reach the nerve terminal without supporting that retrieval.

evidence.snippet: Patients with mutations in ZNF711 all present with mild to moderate ID and poor speech accompanied by additional features in some patients, including autistic features and mild facial dysmorphisms, suggesting that ZNF711 mutations cause non-syndromic ID.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the phenotype and the authors' non-syndromic assignment recorded in these notes.

evidence.snippet: Furthermore, PHF8 interacts with another XMLR protein, ZNF711, which binds to a subset of PHF8 target genes, including the XLMR gene JARID1C.
evidence.explanation: Source for describing ZNF711 as a chromatin-associated transcription factor and for its functional link to two other X-linked intellectual disability genes. Quoted verbatim, including the source's "XMLR" typographical error.

evidence.snippet: The screen has discovered nine genes implicated in XLMR, including SYP, ZNF711 and CASK reported here, confirming the power of this strategy.
evidence.explanation: The 208-family resequencing screen that first implicated ZNF711, cited here so the claim in these notes does not depend on an evidence item attached to a different row.

genes/15.notes: ZNF711, a chromatin-associated transcription factor that interacts with the X-linked intellectual disability protein PHF8 and binds a subset of PHF8 target genes. Implicated by the 208-family X-chromosome resequencing screen and confirmed in two large four-generation pedigrees. Affected males have mild to moderate intellectual disability with poor speech; autistic features and mild facial dysmorphism occur in some but not all patients.

evidence.snippet: We report a novel missense mutation (c.1040G>A, p.Arg347Gln) in MID2, which encodes ubiquitin ligase E3, as the likely cause of X-linked mental retardation in a large kindred.
evidence.explanation: The gene assignment, preserving the authors' "likely cause" hedge.

evidence.snippet: When transiently expressed in HEK293T cell line, the mutation was found to abolish the function of the COS domain in the protein.
evidence.explanation: Source for the molecular consequence recorded in these notes.

genes/16.notes: Midline 2, an E3 ubiquitin ligase. The reported causal allele abolishes the function of the protein's COS domain, and the mutant protein accumulates in the cytoplasm instead of binding the cytoskeleton. The assignment rests on a single large kindred plus one further variant from a 480-individual screen, and has no ClinGen gene-disease validity curation.

evidence.snippet: In the poorly characterized KLHL15 gene, encoding a member of the kelch-like protein family, we identified a protein-truncating variant
evidence.explanation: The causal allele class identified in this gene by the discovery study.

evidence.snippet: KLHL15-Cul3 specifically targets a brain-specific regulatory subunit of the protein phosphatase 2A (PP2A/B'ß) and thereby promotes its proteasomal degradation, resulting in the formation of alternative PP2A holoenzymes.
evidence.explanation: Source for the molecular function recorded in these notes.

genes/17.notes: Kelch-like family member 15, a substrate adaptor for Cul3-based E3 ubiquitin ligases that targets a brain-specific regulatory subunit of protein phosphatase 2A for proteasomal degradation. Identified by X-exome sequencing of 405 unresolved families, with supporting evidence from a second family carrying a partial gene deletion. No ClinGen gene-disease validity curation exists for this gene.

evidence.snippet: Mutations include deletion of an entire coding exon, a nonsense mutation, a frame-shift mutation resulting in premature termination of translation, and a missense mutation involving a highly conserved amino acid residue neighboring FRMPD4-FERM domain.
evidence.explanation: The allele spectrum recorded in these notes.

evidence.snippet: FRMPD4 (FERM and PDZ Domain Containing 4) is a neural scaffolding protein that interacts with PSD-95 to positively regulate dendritic spine morphogenesis, and with mGluR1/5 and Homer to regulate mGluR1/5 signaling.
evidence.explanation: Source for the protein function recorded in these notes.
